# asyntai_website_settings (Resource)

Widget settings of one website: the same settings as the Customize page of the dashboard, for example `ai_support_name`, `widget_color` or `welcome_message`.

Terraform manages only the settings you list. Every other setting keeps its current value. Write each value as text: `true`, `42` and `"#0f172a"` all work. For a list setting such as `reply_languages`, use `jsonencode(["en", "de"])`.

Your plan decides which settings you can change. The API refuses a setting your plan cannot change, and then saves nothing. `all_settings_json` shows every setting and its current value.

~> `terraform destroy` removes this resource from the Terraform state only. The settings keep their values.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "asyntai_website_settings" "shop" {
  website_id = asyntai_website.shop.id

  settings = {
    ai_support_name = "Ava"
    widget_color    = "#0f172a"
    use_emoji       = true
    reply_languages = jsonencode(["en", "de"])
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `settings` (Map of String) The settings to manage, as `name = value`.
- `website_id` (String) Id of the website, for example `asyntai_website.main.id`.

### Read-Only

- `all_settings_json` (String) Every setting of the website and its current value, as JSON. Use `jsondecode()` to read it.
- `id` (String) Same as `website_id`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by website id. Then list the settings you want Terraform to manage.
terraform import asyntai_website_settings.shop 42
```
